thread:
maya li: quick RFC follow-up — we need to decide the canonical place for cost attribution tags (pre-enrich vs post-enrich). yesterday's doc left the boundary fuzzy and it's causing conflicting assumptions in storage and query layers.
kevin r: agreed. main tradeoff is: pre-enrich attribution means cheaper storage + simpler queries, but we lose some accuracy when late enrichment adds tenant/billing info.
samir: do we have numbers on how often late enrichment actually changes billing keys? even rough % would help tradeoff.
maya li: from sampling last month ~ 4.8% of traces got billing ATTR added post-ingest. but the delta matters because those 4.8% are often expensive, long-running traces.
nora: if we anchor billing pre-enrich, customers will see under-attribution for those long traces. Ops hates surprises.
kevin r: proposal: keep a lightweight pre-enrich billing hint (billing_hint) that's sticky, and allow post-enrich to override using a deterministic reconciliation job that updates aggregated counters. That keeps ingest low-latency but enables eventual correctness.
maya li: sounds reasonable. how does this affect the query surface? we can't make users confused by counters changing later.
samir: we should expose two counters: billed_by_ingest and billed_final. UI shows billed_by_ingest as the low-latency number and billed_final with a TTL (e.g., finalizes within 24h). docs explain eventual reconciliation.
ops-bot: deploy-notify: reconciliation-job scheduled to run daily at 03:00 UTC if approved :gear:
kevin r: implementation notes: store billing_hint as a top-level attr on the envelope (string), and post-enrich writes final_billing_key into enrichment output. Reconciler will join enrichment artifacts to envelope id and update materialized aggregates.
maya li: putting billing_hint top-level increases envelope size slightly. estimate: +16 bytes avg, means ~0.4% storage increase. acceptable?
nora: +0.4% is fine compared to under-billing risk. need a flag for customers who want strictly deterministic billing at ingest though (enterprise).
samir: for the reconciler join we need a stable envelope_id across pipeline handoffs. are we happy with current envelope_id TTL and dedupe semantics?
kevin r: yes but we should strengthen invariants: envelope_id must be canonical and preserved by all prefetch/proxy sidecars. I'll open a tiny change to enforcement middleware.
maya li: also we need an audit trail for overrides — add an enum override_reason and who-triggered. keeps compliance happy.
nora: +1 audit trail. and add a metric for "reconciliations_applied" to watch churn.
samir: quick config snippet for the heuristic I proposed:
```
# enricher config snippet
apply_billing_override: true
override_policy: prefer_post_enrich_if_confidence_gt: 0.85
```
kevin r: we need to standardize confidence score semantics across enrichers or reconciliation will be fuzzy. Document: confidence in [0,1], >=0.85 accepted.
maya li: action items: 1) kevin enforce envelope_id invariant (PR) 2) samir add billed_by_ingest/billed_final in schema + metrics 3) nora docs and enterprise opt-in flag 4) kevin/nora add audit fields. I'll compile short addendum to the RFC and push to the repo.
kevin r: will do.
nora: will draft docs.
ops-bot: reminder: weekly-ops sync tomorrow 10:00 — add reconciliation rollout to agenda.
maya li: thanks all — if no objections I'll push RFC addendum by EOD.
kevin r: fine by me :thumbsup:
samir: good enough, let's iterate post-rollout. :+1:
